title: Quantum-biology demos: a governed quantum pipeline and a bioprocess yardstick
description:
Two small, runnable demonstrations of placing a computational step inside a governed biology workflow.

The first reproduces QuASeR's de novo assembly as QAOA on PennyLane (three reads, nine qubits, verified against brute force), trains a variational quantum classifier downstream of it, and places both behind a dataset-descriptor runtime and a gateway with admission control, rate limiting, a circuit-identity cache and an event record.

The second is a mechanistic fed-batch CHO bioreactor model under a contract of in-process limits, with a search controller that chooses a feed plan from 256 candidates and writes an attributed decision artifact.

Neither claims quantum advantage: every instance is small enough to check classically, and make check asserts each stated result. Independent work, unaffiliated with the author's employer. Discussed at BOF-2099, IEEE Quantum Week 2026; not an IEEE publication.
